THE IDEA
In 1930, Tombaugh found Pluto by blinking two plates
A blink comparator flicks between two photographs of the same sky. Every star stays put; the one that moved jumps out at the eye.
BLINK rebuilds that machine for SPHEREx: a billion objects, 102 colours, in any browser.
BLINK · SPHEREx Time Machine

THE PRODUCT
From one click to a discovery report
01 · CLICK
Pick any point
Click anywhere on the all-sky SPHEREx mosaic.
02 · FIND
Every exposure
IRSA’s SIA2 service lists all exposures covering that point.
03 · BLINK
One common grid
Frames are reprojected north-up and played in a timeline.
04 · DIFFERENCE
Static stars cancel
Subtract the median sky; peaks of 5σ or more are listed as detections.
05 · CROSS-MATCH
Known or new?
JPL labels each catalogued asteroid and comet in every frame.
06 · REPORT
Spectrum and report
A 0.75–5 µm spectrum, plus coordinates, epochs and photometry in one copy.
BLINK · SPHEREx Time Machine

HOW NASA DATA MAKES IT POSSIBLE
A thin server between the browser and NASA’s open data
Browser
Plain JavaScript modules, Aladin Lite sky map, no installs or logins
BLINK server
Node 20 + Fastify, a 140-line FITS reader, TAN-SIP WCS, disk cache
IRSA SIA2
Exposure catalogue
AWS Open Data
Raw FITS files
NASA/JPL SSD
Horizons and SBDB
CDS
HiPS mosaics, Sesame
Why a server: upstream services send no CORS headers, repeats hit a disk cache, NASA sees one request instead of many.
